newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's BDI demands tax relief for industry.
newsitem.headline: Germany's BDI demands tax relief for industry.

text.p: German industry needs immediate action to relieve its fiscal burdens following the failure of the government's planned tax reform, Federation of German Industry (BDI) president Hans-Olaf Henkel said on Wednesday.
"The government's tax reform plans aroused expectations among investors," Henkel said in an interview with the news magazine Wirtschafts Woche. "Now, investment decisions are passing us by.
Industry needs lower taxes, or more jobs will move abroad, he said.
"Without tax reform, the goal of halving unemployment by 2000 is unachievable," Henkel said, adding the business sector could not wait until the next elections scheduled for September 1998.

The lower house of parliament voted on Tuesday to relaunch the government's tax reforms after they were blocked by the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) in parliament's conflict-resolution process, but many observers consider the proposal dead.

Deputies from Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition voted to overturn a decision by the SPD-controlled parliamentary mediation committee to reject its plan for sweeping cuts in income and corporate taxes.
But Henkel said further meetings of parliament's mediation committee were unlikely to achieve much, Henkel said.
Targeted initiatives for smaller reforms could be more successful than further government efforts to achieve its comprehensive tax reform, he said.
